title: Work backwards
objective: Solve a problem by starting from the goal and undoing one step at a time.

sources.title: Pólya, How to Solve It (Princeton University Press): heuristics for problem solving, including breaking a problem into parts and working backwards

simplifies: Here working backwards always finds the fewest presses (the tests check this against a full search up to 600). For many problems it only narrows the choices, which is still a big help.

quiz.prompt: With +1 and ×2 starting from 1, what's the fewest presses to reach 16?

options.explanation: Right. 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 16: four doublings. Working back, 16 halves straight down to 1.
That's pressing +1 fifteen times. Doubling gets there much faster.
Backwards: 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 is four undos, so four presses.

quiz.prompt: Why is working backwards easier here than working forwards?

options.text: Backwards there's usually only one sensible undo at each step
options.explanation: Right. Forwards, every number offers two choices; backwards, odd numbers must have come from +1 and even ones are best halved.
Speed isn't the point; the number of choices is.

options.text: It isn't: both are equally hard
options.explanation: Forwards branches at every step, so there are far more paths to consider.
